title: solo dev here releasing my game, Conquest Online, to the public for our Open Alpha Playtest.
author: Unfair-Frosting-4934

replies.author: DaleRobinson
replies.body: it matches the laziness of using emojis, I guess

replies.author: New-Part-6917
replies.body: At a glance, If the gameplay and mechanics have been well designed (which is presumably what he is trying to get feedback on now) swapping out assets is not difficult and would be an immediate difference. Hopefully you have spent a lot of time on the foundations, looks like an ambitious project. Good luck.

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body:
Thank you for actual feedback.

I cant believe people cant get past that. I guess to hook people in long enough to pay attention for real I need to make it pretty.

replies.author: joeban1
replies.body:
Even at alpha you cannot be going to playtest leaving default models like that in. 

That is even worse than the bare minimum

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body:
How is one supposed to get actual real time debugging without other player input? If I wanted criticisms on the art I would have asked "Does this art style look good?" 

I don't think others understand the rate at which development can be halted. If I spent the entirety of time just making it look as good and polished as possible there would be even less barebones gameplay and people would complain. I have entire questing system, party mechanics, gem socketing, item upgrading, world bosses...   
  
Yet people are like "ew low poly" 

I can see why the industry has suffered.

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body: I mean they aren't even models .. It's literally the default models the Ai used. I haven't updated any visuals yet because I am working on functionality .....

comments.author: Voiston44
comments.body:
Hey, you've customized your UI so little that we recognize at first glance that it's Claude's work. Not from GPT / Gemini or others, we can literally guess that it's Claude.

It's fine to focus on features first, and I'm not against using AI—quite the opposite—but when you present a game made by AI, for me there's a kind of unspoken agreement with the player: "I used AI, but I thought about it and designed it myself; it's not random. I CHOSE what I'm offering you here, even if it's AI-powered." I don't see myself in that.

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body: Have you even tried the game?

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body: Yes, a little, and as proof, your Whirlwind skill, for example, is applied to the enemy instead of originating from the player. You lose the surround-effect of the skill if you target an enemy in front of you and have enemies behind you. Is this the intended behavior? In any case, I may have been harsh in my first message, and I apologize if it offended you.

replies.author: xthrowxawayx420
replies.body: Your game is not ready to be shared. And if you can’t handle feedback at all, you are wasting your time with this project.
